title: Engine ragdoll module — Rapier-based template + spawn/sync/teardown systems under engine/physics/ragdoll/
intent: Build a reusable engine module that turns any project's skeleton-with-meshes into a Rapier physics ragdoll on demand. Projects register a `RagdollTemplate` (bodies + joints) at bootstrap. To activate, a project writes `RagdollSpawnRequest { templateKey, impulse? }` on a skeleton entity; the engine spawns Rapier rigid bodies + constraints, re-parents the visible meshes from animation pivots to physics bodies, and disables animation systems for that entity via a `RagdollActive` marker. `RagdollSyncSystem` copies Rapier transforms to ECS Transforms every fixedUpdate. `RagdollTeardownSystem` disposes Rapier bodies + joints when the skeleton root is despawned or an explicit teardown request fires. Full design rationale + schema + first-consumer mapping in `docs/game-design/ragdoll-module-design.md`. Replaces the S105 procedural-spring path that lived (incorrectly) inside `examples/kaboom-crew/`.
rationale: Source: `docs/game-design/ragdoll-module-design.md` (this batch) + memory [project-ragdoll-physics-module]. The S105 spring-based ragdoll worked but lives in the wrong place — project-specific code inside `examples/kaboom-crew/src/`, when it should be a generic engine primitive (per CLAUDE.md 'engine ships only generic primitives + reusable systems'). Rapier is already integrated for physics-bench + Beacon World character controller; the ragdoll module is the natural next physics surface. First consumer is Kaboom Crew (paired story GDP-2026-05-24-002); future consumers are Beacon World drones + any humanoid-character sample. Marked `should` because the current ragdoll WORKS (S105 + S108); this is correctness-of-placement work, not a blocker. Multiplayer Sprint B (GDP-2026-05-22-011, MUST) should ship first.
acceptanceHints: READ FIRST: `docs/game-design/ragdoll-module-design.md` — the canonical spec. Schema, system responsibilities, first-consumer template breakdown all live there. This story is the implementation contract for that doc.

DIRECTORY: NEW `engine/physics/ragdoll/`. Sits alongside the existing Rapier integration (whichever directory currently holds the physics-step + body-spawn primitives — dev places ragdoll module as a sibling).
SCHEMA FILES (under `schemas/components/`):
ragdoll-template.schema.json — RagdollTemplate with bodies[] + joints[] + optional defaults
ragdoll-spawn-request.schema.json — RagdollSpawnRequest { templateKey, impulse? }
ragdoll-state.schema.json — RagdollState { templateKey, spawnedAt, bodyEntities map, jointEntities[] }
ragdoll-body.schema.json — RagdollBody { ownerRoot, bodyName, rapierBodyHandle } per body entity
All schemas validate via the existing project-check pipeline.
TEMPLATE REGISTRY (engine/physics/ragdoll/template-registry.ts):
`registerRagdollTemplate(key: string, template: RagdollTemplate): void` — throws on duplicate key
`getRagdollTemplate(key: string): RagdollTemplate | undefined`
`listRagdollTemplates(): string[]` — for engine doctor + debug probes
Templates are JSON-schema-validated on registration; bad templates throw with field path.
SYSTEMS (engine/physics/ragdoll/):

`createRagdollSpawnSystem()` — consumes RagdollSpawnRequest; spawns Rapier bodies (RigidBodyType.Dynamic) + Rapier joints per the template; spawns ECS body entities with Transform + RagdollBody + MeshRenderer (mesh handle moved from the animated mesh entity); writes RagdollState on the root; writes RagdollActive marker on the root; deletes the request.
`createRagdollSyncSystem()` — runs after the Rapier step every fixedUpdate; for each RagdollState root, copies each body's Rapier transform back to its body entity's Transform.

`createRagdollTeardownSystem()` — disposes Rapier bodies + joints on RagdollTeardownRequest (explicit) or on root entity despawn (cascading); cleans up body + joint entities; removes RagdollState + RagdollActive.
All three systems are project-agnostic — they do not reference any specific game.

MESH HANDOVER: when a ragdoll spawns, the visible meshes of the skeleton are RE-PARENTED — their parent Transform changes from the animation pivot entities to the corresponding ragdoll body entities. This is the only invasive bit of the spawn: the spawn system must know which mesh entities correspond to which body names. Mechanism: the project's spawn-time wiring writes a `SkeletalBinding { bodyName }` component on each mesh entity; the spawn system reads it. Generic across humanoid / drone / vehicle.

RAPIER COLLISION GROUPS: ragdoll bodies use a new `RAGDOLL_BODY` collision group. By default, exclude collisions with itself + with bombs/pickups/live bombers. Include collisions with `ARENA_WALL` + `ARENA_FLOOR`. Project can override on registration (e.g. a vehicle ragdoll might collide with itself).
JOINT IMPLEMENTATION:
spherical → Rapier `SphericalJoint` + angular limit configuration (cone + twist)
revolute  → Rapier `RevoluteJoint` + min/max angular limit
fixed     → Rapier `FixedJoint`
Optional spring stiffness/damping per joint via Rapier's joint motor with spring config.
DEFAULTS — applied per template's `defaults?` block when a body/joint omits an explicit override:
linearDamping: 0.4, angularDamping: 0.6, coneLimit: π/2, twistLimit: π/4
All overridable per-body/per-joint.

INTERNAL EXAMPLE FOR TESTING: a fixture under tests/fixtures/ragdoll/ — 3-body Y-shape skeleton (a torso + two arms, one revolute, one spherical) with a simple template. Unit tests assert spawn produces 3 body entities + 2 joint entities; sync copies Rapier transform to ECS each tick; teardown disposes everything cleanly.
DOCTOR INTEGRATION: engine doctor's existing project scan gains a 'Ragdoll module' section. Lines:
'Ragdoll templates: N registered ([template-keys])'
'Active ragdolls: M' (counts entities with RagdollState component)
Warning if M > 16: 'Active ragdoll count high — potential leak'.
UNIT TESTS (tests/unit/engine/physics/ragdoll/):
template-registry: register/lookup/list, duplicate-key error.
schema validation: malformed templates reject with field path.
spawn-system: 3-body fixture spawns 3 ECS body entities + 2 joint entities; meshes re-parent; RagdollActive marker written.
sync-system: simulated Rapier body position → ECS Transform mirrors it.
teardown-system: dispose path clears all bodies/joints/components.
collision-group: ragdoll-vs-ragdoll filtered; ragdoll-vs-arena enabled.

INTEGRATION TEST: a synthetic scene with the Y-shape fixture: spawn → wait 1 second of fixedUpdate steps → assert bodies have moved (gravity took effect); apply teardown request → assert bodies despawned.
DETERMINISM: existing Rapier seeding pattern. Same template + same fixed dt + same impulse → same trajectory. The engine module adds nothing that breaks Rapier's determinism guarantees.

PERFORMANCE BUDGET: per-spawn cost = O(bodies + joints), one-time. Per-fixedUpdate cost = Rapier-native (one body update + one constraint solve per body/joint). At 36 bodies + 36 joints worst case (4 ragdolls): well under physics-bench's 200-rigid-body benchmark.

DOES NOT TOUCH: engine/render (mesh re-parenting works via the existing Transform.parent chain — no renderer changes), engine/core/ecs (just consumes existing component pipeline), any project source. Pure additive engine surface.
OUT OF SCOPE (explicit):
Skinned-mesh ragdolls (no rig binding; only node-tree-of-primitives skeletons).
Active ragdoll / motor-driven joints.
Soft-body, cloth, hair.
Reverse handover (ragdoll → animated) — API doesn't lock it out but no implementation in v1.
Dismemberment (joint break on impact force).
Per-impact audio coupling.
Replicating ragdoll state over network — clients run their own local sims per gameplay-systems.md §12.1.
